name: howto
title: The Levoit Core 300-P in five minutes
sub: From the box to clean air in six steps, taken from the manual and Levoit's own guides
footer: Sources: Levoit Core 300 user manual; Levoit's filter, maintenance and room-size guides; EPA wildfire filtration factsheet (June 2026).

items.head: Unwrap the filter first
items.body: Twist off the base cover, pull the filter out, remove the plastic bag it ships in, and seat it back in. Running it wrapped is a common cause of a rattle.

items.head: Give it 15 inches of space
items.body: The manual asks for 15 in (38 cm) of clearance on every side. It pulls air in around the bottom and blows it out the top, so not in a corner, not under a shelf.

items.head: One room, door closed
items.body: Sized for about 219 sq ft at 4.8 air changes an hour. Put it where you spend the most hours, usually the bedroom, and keep the door shut.

items.head: High by day, Sleep at night
items.body: Speed 3 cleans fastest; Sleep mode is the quiet setting (24 dB by Levoit's spec). Tap the display button so the panel light goes dark at night.

items.head: Vacuum the outside monthly
items.body: The mesh pre-filter is the outer layer of the cylinder. A gentle pass with the vacuum brush every 1–3 months keeps airflow up. Never wash the filter.

items.head: New filter at 6–8 months
items.body: When the Check Filter light comes on, fit a genuine Core 300-RF, then hold the button 3 seconds until the light goes out. It is a timer, not a sensor.
